notes: Science descriptions and photo provenance for EVA-09 through EVA-12 reviewed by Kelly. Stop names describe proposed EVA observations, not official geologic target names. Status ready refers to science metadata; route order and minutes remain team planning estimates, and H2-H4 remain candidate habitats. Positions remain projected metres, converted by area.json. EVA-07 and EVA-08 retain their own data files. See data/processed/scenario-science/REVIEW.md.

H1.name: Habitat H1
H1.note: Confirmed team habitat: start of EVA-07 and EVA-09, and the drive start for EVA-08. About 3° slope.

H2.name: Habitat H2
H2.note: Flat-site candidate from the 6 km terrain script (area.json habitatCandidates[0]); mean slope 3.7° over about 100 m. North-west of the boxwork.

H3.name: Habitat H3
H3.note: Flat-site candidate from the 6 km terrain script (area.json habitatCandidates[1]); mean slope 4.1° over about 100 m. East of the boxwork.

H4.name: Habitat H4
H4.note: Flat-site candidate from the 6 km terrain script (area.json habitatCandidates[2]); mean slope 4.4° over about 100 m. North-east of the boxwork, east of the Gediz Vallis stops.

scenarios.name: The Southern Traverse
scenarios.label: EVA-09 · H1 South
scenarios.summary: From H1 north-east into the boxwork, then south along Curiosity's late-2025 and 2026 drive.

stops.name: Southern Outcrop Survey
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4752 waypoint. Compare exposed bedrock, fractures and loose surface material in the southern traverse panorama. Record textures before comparing them with the later stops; the image alone does not identify minerals.
stops.why: Document the starting bedrock textures for comparison along the southern traverse.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 4752. NASA 360-degree cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

stops.name: Campo Marte Context
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4893 waypoint. NASA reports that the Campo Marte drilling campaign investigated layered sulfate-unit rock above the boxwork. Use this waypoint to compare visible layering and block textures with the first stop. The panorama provides landscape context, not a verified position of the drill hole.
stops.why: Relate visible rock layers to the published Campo Marte investigation without inferring mineral abundance from the photo.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 4893. NASA 360-degree cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

stops.name: Layer Relationships
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4977 waypoint. Compare layer orientations and look for places where one set of layers truncates another. NASA describes cross-bedding and layer contacts during this part of the traverse. The illustration shows APXS at Tunas Khasa on the earlier sol 4976 workspace; it is contextual, not a photograph of this precise stop.
stops.why: Record layer relationships that can help distinguish deposition from later erosion.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view / earlier workspace context. Front Hazcam, sol 4976, 03:01:56 UTC: APXS at Tunas Khasa. The stop is the sol 4977 waypoint after further driving, not this photographed target; distance is unverified.

stops.name: Disc Texture Comparison
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 5021 waypoint. Optional comparison of bedrock textures farther south. NASA reported disc-shaped features at Salar de Vacas on sol 5016, before driving onward. That earlier close-up illustrates a question to investigate, not a confirmed feature at this coordinate. Shape alone does not establish which mineral formed the discs.
stops.why: If time permits, compare local textures with the earlier disc-bearing rock while keeping mineral identification open.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view / earlier workspace context. MAHLI focus merge, sol 5016, 02:14:02 UTC: disc-shaped features at Salar de Vacas. This is not the sol 5021 coordinate; distance is unverified.

scenarios.name: The North-West Traverse
scenarios.label: EVA-10 · H2
scenarios.summary: From H2 east to Curiosity's early-2025 drive out of Gediz Vallis, then north to a 54-sol stop from late 2023.

stops.name: Western Bedrock Survey
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4456 waypoint. Use the landscape panorama to document exposed rock, broken blocks and surface cover. Compare fracture spacing and block shapes with the next stop. These are proposed observations at a rover waypoint, not evidence that a particular mineral was sampled here.
stops.why: Establish a bedrock and surface-cover comparison for the north-west traverse.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 4456. NASA 360-degree cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

stops.name: Butte and Bedrock Context
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4417 waypoint. Compare foreground rocks with the layered hills in the background. Record which observations concern nearby bedrock and which concern distant outcrops. The accompanying multi-sol panorama combines sols 4417 through 4423 and is a context view, not a single exposure precisely registered to this stop.
stops.why: Connect local rock observations with the larger exposed layers without treating distant outcrops as samples at the stop.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view / multi-sol context. NASA panorama assembled from sols 4417–4423, at site 112, drive 1014. It includes the stop sol but is not a single exposure registered to its coordinate; distance is unverified.

stops.name: Sequoia Drill Context
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 3974 waypoint. Optional observation near the Sequoia investigation. NASA identified Sequoia as the next drill target after the sol 3974 positioning move. Compare the surrounding light-toned bedrock with earlier stops. This panorama is landscape context; it does not locate the drill hole or provide a mineral analysis.
stops.why: Compare the published Sequoia drill context with bedrock observations from the rest of this traverse.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 3974. NASA 360-degree cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

scenarios.name: The Boxwork Approach
scenarios.label: EVA-11 · H3
scenarios.summary: From H3 west along the route Curiosity drove into the boxwork in spring 2025.

stops.name: Boxwork Approach Panorama
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4507 waypoint. Document the broad landscape on the approach to the boxwork. NASA describes imaging distant potential boxwork structures during this part of the drive. Record the relationship between foreground blocks and distant relief; this waypoint is not a surveyed ridge sampling site.
stops.why: Establish the landscape context before examining the smaller fracture patterns farther along the approach.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 4507. NASA 360-degree cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

stops.name: Fracture Pattern Survey
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4527 waypoint. Photograph exposed blocks and trace visible fractures where they can be followed. Compare their orientations and spacing with the approach panorama. Fractures visible in an image are not by themselves proof of groundwater cement or a specific mineral.
stops.why: Measure visible fracture patterns for comparison with the later boxwork context.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 4527. NASA 360-degree cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

stops.name: Bedrock Texture Comparison
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4548 waypoint. Compare rough and smooth surfaces, block edges and loose cover with the earlier fracture-survey stop. Keep observations separate from explanations: differences in appearance can guide later sampling but do not establish composition.
stops.why: Look for changes in bedrock texture along the boxwork approach.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 4548. NASA 360-degree cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

stops.name: Boxwork Trough Context
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4575 waypoint. Optional landscape comparison at the end of the approach. NASA describes a trough and fractured terrain during sol 4575 operations in the boxwork region. Compare linear features with the earlier fracture survey. The waypoint is an observation location, not a verified position of any named contact-science target.
stops.why: Compare the boxwork-region trough context with fracture patterns observed earlier in the walk.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 4575. NASA 360-degree cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

scenarios.name: The North-East Traverse
scenarios.label: EVA-12 · H4
scenarios.summary: From H4 west to waypoints Curiosity visited in 2022 and 2023.

stops.name: Rock and Sand Comparison
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 3878 waypoint. Compare exposed rock with loose material between the blocks. Record grain-size differences only where the image resolves them, and note shadows that can hide textures. The partial panorama supplies local context, not a chemical measurement.
stops.why: Document how surface cover changes which bedrock textures can be observed.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 3878. NASA 118-degree partial cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

stops.name: Layered Block Survey
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 3815 waypoint. Inspect visible block edges and layering, and compare them with the first stop. Record candidate surfaces for a closer look rather than assigning an official target name or claiming that a drill sample was taken at this coordinate.
stops.why: Compare exposed rock textures and layering across the north-east traverse.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 3815. NASA 220-degree partial cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

stops.name: Ripple and Bedrock Context
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 3749 waypoint. Compare rippled loose material with exposed bedrock in the panorama. Record where sand hides rock boundaries and where erosion exposes them. The image is an observation aid; it does not determine grain chemistry or the age of the deposits.
stops.why: Distinguish loose wind-shaped surface cover from exposed rock.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 3749. NASA 316-degree partial cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

stops.name: Northern Surface Panorama
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 3608 waypoint. Optional final comparison using the northern panorama. Record block shapes, exposed surfaces and patches of loose material, then compare them with the previous stops. Any proposed sampling remains an EVA activity, not a claim that Curiosity performed it here.
stops.why: Complete the traverse-wide comparison of bedrock exposure and surface cover if the return reserve allows.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Right Navcam, sol 3608. NASA 360-degree cylindrical panorama from the same recorded sol as the waypoint. Camera pose and photo footprint have not been registered to the MarsWay map; the depicted rocks are not surveyed sample points. Black areas contain no image data.

science_review.summary: Kelly-reviewed proposed science observations at Curiosity waypoints; NASA photos with camera, sol and source. Habitat approval and operational timing remain separate.
